chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whose half of his wealth is in cash (ayn) and half is in debts (dayn), so Zakat becomes due upon him. He said: 'He should pay Zakat on the cash and leave the debt.' I said: 'What if he collects it after six months?' He said: 'He should pay Zakat on it when he collects it.' I said: 'What if a year passes for him and the month in which he usually pays Zakat arrives, and for half his wealth a year has passed, and for the other half six months have passed?' He said: 'He should pay Zakat on that upon which a year has passed, and leave the other until a year passes for it.' I said: 'What if he desires to pay Zakat on that (the other half) as well?' He said: 'How good that is!'

key_terms.الْحَوْل: The lunar year period for Zakat liability
key_terms.عَيْن: Cash or tangible assets held directly

ai.seo_question: How does one calculate and pay Zakat when half of their wealth is in cash and half is in outstanding debts?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudence of 'Hawl al-Ayn' (annual cycle of the asset), establishing that cash and debt are assessed independently regarding their one-year holding period. It highlights the scholarly principle that Zakat is not levied on the debt itself but on the recovered value once it becomes a tangible asset, while also encouraging voluntary early payment as a meritorious act.
